question.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ |
| $X=2$ | $0$ | $0.65$ |

Calculate the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
The covariance of two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint support $S$ is defined as

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])(y-\text{E}[Y])f(x,y).
$$

First, let's find the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y.$ These are given by the row and column totals, respectively.

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=4$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ | $0.35$ |
| $X=2$ | $0$ | $0.65$ | $0.65$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.1$ | $0.9$ | $1$ |

We now compute $\text{E}[X]$ and $\text{E}[Y],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}x\cdot {f}_{X}(x) \\  & =0\cdot 0.35+2\cdot 0.65 \\  & =0+1.3 \\  & =1.3 \\ \text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}y\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =1\cdot 0.1+4\cdot 0.9 \\  & =0.1+3.6 \\  & =3.7\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for the covariance, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])(y-\text{E}[Y])f(x,y) \\  & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-1.3)(y-3.7)f(x,y) \\  & =(0-1.3)(1-3.7)f(0,1) \\  & +(0-1.3)(4-3.7)f(0,4) \\  & +(2-1.3)(1-3.7)f(2,1) \\  & +(2-1.3)(4-3.7)f(2,4) \\  & =(-1.3)(-2.7)(0.1) \\  & +(-1.3)(0.3)(0.25) \\  & +(0.7)(-2.7)(0) \\  & +(0.7)(0.3)(0.65) \\  & =0.39.\end{aligned}
$$
